edges.effect_quant: Tamoxifen has some of the strongest breast-cancer chemoprevention evidence in the corpus. In the NSABP P-1 trial it reduced invasive breast cancer by 49%, and longer-horizon pooled SERM data show a durable overall reduction in breast-cancer incidence among higher-risk women.
edges.population: women at elevated breast-cancer risk, including those with increased Gail-model risk, atypical hyperplasia, LCIS, or other high-risk prevention-trial eligibility features
edges.mechanism: Tamoxifen is a selective estrogen receptor modulator that antagonizes estrogen signaling in breast tissue, lowering the development of estrogen receptor-positive incident cancers in higher-risk women.
edges.summary: Among preventive endocrine options, tamoxifen remains one of the clearest protective edges. The randomized prevention-trial evidence is direct, the effect size is clinically meaningful, and the main uncertainty is not whether it works but which higher-risk women judge the benefit worth the known adverse-effect tradeoffs.
edges.caveats: The benefit is strongest for estrogen receptor-positive disease and does not imply universal prevention across all breast-cancer subtypes. Endometrial cancer, thromboembolic risk, and menopausal symptoms are major tradeoffs that are not represented by this incidence-focused edge.
